## claude.ai Data Insights
Honeycomb Insights MCP Server — Business Data Query Interface

Backs a curated mart layer (dbt models over Snowflake) that answers business
questions about Honeycomb: usage, billing, marketing, sales, customer health.

IMPORTANT: Follow this workflow for best results:

1. ORIENT with the mart map:
   - Call `list_models` with no arguments to see the full mart landscape
     grouped by domain.
   - Each result has a `purpose` (one-line) and `use_cases` (answer-shaped
     phrases) — skim these to find models that plausibly answer the question.
   - Note `row_count` and `last_modified` for size and freshness context.

2. NARROW to a specific model:
   - When the user names a field or metric ("ARR", "DAU",
     "salesforce_account_id"), use `search_columns(pattern="...")` to locate
     which models carry that column.
   - When the user describes a concept ("revenue by customer segment"), use
     `list_models(pattern="...")` to match against
     name/purpose/description/use_cases.
   - Both tools take a `pattern` argument — a case-insensitive Python
     regex. They rank name hits above body hits, so the top result is
     usually the right one.
   - Both tools return a page: `{total, offset, limit, items}` (default
     limit: 200 models / 100 column matches). If `total` exceeds
     `offset + len(items)`, results were truncated — narrow the pattern or
     call again with `offset=offset+limit`.

3. UNDERSTAND the chosen model BEFORE writing SQL:
   - Call `get_model_details(model_name)` to fetch columns (with types,
     descriptions, optional enum_values), `grain` (uniqueness key), `joins`
     (fact→dim relationships with key mappings), and full `description`
     prose (caveats, exclusions, "use this vs that" guidance).
   - Call this for every model you plan to reference in a query, including
     all joined dimension tables. Never assume column names — verify them
     here first.
   - Read the `description` carefully. Many models document scope limits
     ("excludes automated queries", "current day is exc… [truncated]

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## honeycomb
Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). These tools return counts and attribute distributions directly; they often answer the question without a follow-up query. Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1. ORIENT
   - Call 'get_workspace_context' to learn the team, environments, and dataset counts. Use the returned environment slug in subsequent calls.

2. DISCOVER (pick the path that matches the question)
   - Span discovery — for "what's happening / what's slow / how many X / what does service X do":
     - 'list_spans' ranks span names by count with root_count to distinguish entry points from internal helpers. Counts here are often the answer to "how many X happened".
     - 'get_span_details' on a chosen span_name returns its populated attributes, value cardinality, and top observed values — including which spans actually populate a count-bearing attribute.
     Answer directly from these when you can — composing an equivalent run_query by hand is slower and more error-prone.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

It represents the conversation as a whole. The vertical axis is _context length_. Three sections in the bar: prior context, context added in the currently highlighted card (this is the token contribution of this card), and context added in all future cards.

When the currently highlighted card is a tool callthat does not add to the context, then there is only a bar (a minimum height) between prior and future context representing the current location. A tool result can show its approximate token contribution. A user input could show its contribution, although probably the minimum bar height will be taller than this.

Usually, this map moves immediately when a new card is selected (no transition). In narrate mode, when I push n or arrow to add to the screen, it animates smoothly, showing the context growing as the conversation lengthens.

Subagents get their own bar to the right of the main bar! When I click on a subagent card or any card representing a subagent's event, then the main bar shows the context added by the subagent as if the subagent's result card was selected. An additional bar appears next to it, representing the subagent context. The subagent's bar has more parts: before the subagent started; context added before the current selected card; current card's token contribution; future context from later cards; extra space that the subagent didn't use. The subagent's context bar should use _the same scale as the main conversation_, unless the subagent's context is larger than the main conversation's, in which case it scales to screen height. The subagent's "context added before" starts at the height of the subagent invocation on the main bar, unless that would make its context summary go off the bottom of the page, in which case it moves up to fit.

## Mount Malleable

_A local web app for shaping the story — edit on the page, not in YAML._

- **Title is editable**

## Mount Interactive

_Three modes, a keyboard map, and narrate. Both items below are known,
deliberately deferred rough edges from the final review — neither is a
correctness bug that needs fixing right now._

- **change narrate shortcut** I want 'n/p' to work for "move to the next/prev assistant/user message" in any mode, and let's make the "narrate mode" shortcut something else. Maybe 's' for story?
- A degraded or bogus `?mode=` value stays in the URL while the body is
  `mode-explore`, and pressing `x` won't clear it — `setMode` early-returns on
  a same-mode call. Cosmetic, but it's the one place the URL and the body
  class disagree.
- Clicking a related-event link in the detail pane during narrate fires
  `hashchange`, and `syncFromHash` selects a card that's still hidden and
  outside the revealed prefix. No error, and it self-heals on the next beat,
  but mid-talk it's a spoiler.

## Maybe later

- **Hooks.** The logs carry a lot of hook detail we currently leave as
  summary-only: `system` events (`stop_hook_summary`, `turn_duration`,
  `hookInfos`, `hookErrors`) and the ~157 `attachment` records that are really
  hook-execution records (`hookName`, `hookEvent`, `command`, `stdout`/`stderr`/
  `exitCode`/`durationMs`). Interesting, not urgent — if we do it, they get
  named schema fields like everything else.

# Subagent subactions in the board (design prototype)

Design-only session: mock up how a subagent's own actions ("subactions") show
up inline in the board, in `assets/design-prototype.html`. No parser/renderer
changes — that's the Mount Complete TODO item ("Subagents inline a spawned
Agent's own story"). This is groundwork for that: settling the look before
wiring real data.

## Decisions

- **Inline in the board**, not detail-pane-only and not a drill-down view. The
  subagent's subactions appear as extra cards right in the main event list,
  nested under the Subagent card.
- **Expanded by default**, with a caret in the gutter to collapse. (Doesn't
  matter for a static prototype which state ships as the default markup —
  what matters is both states are designed and the caret affordance exists.)
- **Indented + connecting rail.** Subaction cards sit indented under the
  Subagent card with a vertical rail linking them, ending in a closing marker
  so the rail doesn't dangle into the next top-level card.
- **Full-size cards, not a condensed echo.** First pass shrank subactions into
  a smaller, flattened `.subaction` div — Jess corrected this: a subaction is
  a real `.card` with its own real `k-*` class (`k-assistant`, `k-tool_call`,
  `k-tool_result`), same size, same `<template class="detail">`, same
  click-to-select behavior as a top-level event. Indentation and the rail are
  the *only* difference. `.subactions` supplies the indent/rail wrapper and
  otherwise gets out of the way; it does not restyle its children.
- Confirmed with `ferrum` (already a project dependency for `bin/check-modes`)
  that clicking a nested subaction card selects it and populates the detail
  pane, same as any top-level card — the first attempt at this check used too
  small a headless window and clicked the wrong element, which looked like a
  real bug until re-tested at the right size.

## Source material

Mocked from the real subagent log `examples/episode-8-before/subagents/agent-ae20659fd0f63295e.jsonl`
(the Explore agent, "Explore timeline/replay features") — real content for
each subaction (assistant text, a `Bash` call, a `Grep` call, their results,
final reply), with real `source.line` numbers into that file. Per the parser's
actual kind-mapping rule, a `text` content block is `assistant_message`
regardless of position — so the subagent's opening narration and its closing
summary are both `k-assistant`, not `k-thinking`.

## Scope

Static HTML/CSS in `assets/design-prototype.html` only (mirrored into
`assets/story.css` if new rules are needed). No JS collapse/expand behavior,
no parser or renderer wiring — those remain the Mount Complete implementation
task.

2	
3	Design-only session (no parser/renderer work) — settled the look of a
4	spawned subagent's own story showing up inline in the board, in
5	`assets/design-prototype.html` + `assets/story.css`. The corresponding
6	implementation task is still open: see Mount Complete's "Subagents inline a
7	spawned Agent's own story" in `TODO.md`. Full rationale is in
8	`notes/2026-07-28-subagent-subactions-design.md`; this note is the
9	session-shaped version — what we tried, what broke, what Jess corrected.
10	
11	## Where it landed
12	
13	- A Subagent card (`k-subagent`, red) expands **inline in the board** —
14	  not detail-pane-only, not a drill-down — into the events the subagent
15	  itself produced.
16	- Subaction cards are **full-size `.card` elements** with their own real
17	  `k-*` kind class (`k-assistant`, `k-tool_call`, `k-tool_result`) — same
18	  size, same `<template class="detail">`, same click-to-select behavior as
19	  a top-level event. Indentation + a connecting rail (`.subactions`
20	  wrapper) are the *only* difference from a top-level card.
21	- Expanded by default; a caret in the gutter (after the "Subagent" label,
22	  not before — see gotcha below) is the collapse affordance. Both states
23	  (expanded "Explore" example, collapsed "general-purpose" example) are
24	  built into the prototype so the pair is visible side by side.
25	- The subagent card itself carries an **Agent badge** (mirrors how a
26	  `tool_call` card badges its tool name) and no token/tool-count badges —
27	  those are detail, already in the Fields section of the detail pane, not
28	  a card-face headline.
29	- The subagent's return value gets its **own top-level, non-indented card**
30	  — a new kind, `k-subagent_result` (same red family as `k-subagent`, same
31	  quiet/background treatment as `k-tool_result`). This represents the real
32	  `Task` tool_result the main log records when the subagent's work is
33	  delivered back to its caller — distinct from both a nested subaction and
34	  a plain `k-tool_result`.
35	
36	## Gotchas (for the real implementation, and for future CSS work here)
37	
38	- **Indentation must not double-count `--gutter-w`.** First pass indented
39	  the `.subactions` wrapper by `var(--gutter-w)` on top of subaction cards
40	  that are themselves full `.card`s — each already reserves its own
41	  `--gutter-w` column internally. Stacking both pushed everything a full
42	  extra column too far right. Landed on: no wrapper margin at all, just

# Session 14: subagent subactions, in the design prototype

Design-only session (no parser/renderer work) — settled the look of a
spawned subagent's own story showing up inline in the board, in
`assets/design-prototype.html` + `assets/story.css`. The corresponding
implementation task is still open: see Mount Complete's "Subagents inline a
spawned Agent's own story" in `TODO.md`. Full rationale is in
`notes/2026-07-28-subagent-subactions-design.md`; this note is the
session-shaped version — what we tried, what broke, what Jess corrected.

## Where it landed

- A Subagent card (`k-subagent`, red) expands **inline in the board** —
  not detail-pane-only, not a drill-down — into the events the subagent
  itself produced.
- Subaction cards are **full-size `.card` elements** with their own real
  `k-*` kind class (`k-assistant`, `k-tool_call`, `k-tool_result`) — same
  size, same `<template class="detail">`, same click-to-select behavior as
  a top-level event. Indentation + a connecting rail (`.subactions`
  wrapper) are the *only* difference from a top-level card.
- Expanded by default; a caret in the gutter (after the "Subagent" label,
  not before — see gotcha below) is the collapse affordance. Both states
  (expanded "Explore" example, collapsed "general-purpose" example) are
  built into the prototype so the pair is visible side by side.
- The subagent card itself carries an **Agent badge** (mirrors how a
  `tool_call` card badges its tool name) and no token/tool-count badges —
  those are detail, already in the Fields section of the detail pane, not
  a card-face headline.
- The subagent's return value gets its **own top-level, non-indented card**
  — a new kind, `k-subagent_result` (same red family as `k-subagent`, same
  quiet/background treatment as `k-tool_result`). This represents the real
  `Task` tool_result the main log records when the subagent's work is
  delivered back to its caller — distinct from both a nested subaction and
  a plain `k-tool_result`.

## Gotchas (for the real implementation, and for future CSS work here)

- **Indentation must not double-count `--gutter-w`.** First pass indented
  the `.subactions` wrapper by `var(--gutter-w)` on top of subaction cards
  that are themselves full `.card`s — each already reserves its own
  `--gutter-w` column internally. Stacking both pushed everything a full
  extra column too far right. Landed on: no wrapper margin at all, just
  the rail's own `padding-left: 20px`.
- **`.gutter` inherits `white-space: nowrap`**, fine for every existing
  one/two-word kind label but it clips a longer one — "Subagent Result"
  ran straight into the body column with no gap. Fixed by scoping
  `white-space: normal` onto `.gutter .kind` specifically, so it wraps
  within the fixed gutter column instead.
- **A "condensed miniature card" for subactions was the wrong instinct.**
  First pass shrank subactions into a smaller flattened `.subaction` div to
  read as "quieter than a real event" — this silently dropped the
  click-to-detail behavior every other card has (no `<template>`, not a
  real `<a class="card">`), and Jess caught it by noticing the detail pane
  never rendered. Corrected to full-size real cards; smaller/different was
  never actually wanted, only the indent + rail.
- When checking behavior instead of just looks, a plain screenshot isn't
  enough — used `ferrum` (already a project dependency for
  `bin/check-modes`) to actually click a card in headless Chrome and read
  back the detail pane's contents. First attempt at that check used too
  small a default window and silently clicked the wrong element, which
  looked like a real bug until re-tested at a large-enough window size.

1	# frozen_string_literal: true
2	
3	require "json"
4	
5	module ConversationStory
6	  # Reads a Claude conversation log (a .jsonl file, one JSON record per line) and
7	  # produces the intermediate "document": a Ruby hash matching the schema in
8	  # notes/intermediate-schema.md, ready to serialize as YAML.
9	  #
10	  # Granularity: ONE event per record (per line). The golden test
11	  # asserts event_count == line count. Splitting an assistant record's blocks
12	  # into separate cards is still out of scope — but every assistant record in
13	  # the example logs carries exactly one content block, so classifying the
14	  # record's `kind` by that block's type (thinking / tool_use / text) is not
15	  # block-splitting, just a finer-grained `kind` for the one block present.
16	  #
17	  # The schema is the contract: known event kinds store only named fields.
18	  # Unrecognized record types fall back to kind `unknown` with `detail.raw` kept
19	  # verbatim, so nothing in the log is silently lost.
20	  class Parser
21	    # top-level record `type` -> schema kind, for types with a fixed kind.
22	    # `user` and `assistant` are refined by content shape (see user_kind /
23	    # assistant_kind). Any type not listed here falls through to `unknown`.
24	    TYPE_TO_KIND = {
25	      "system"                => "system",
26	      "attachment"            => "attachment",
27	      "file-history-snapshot" => "file_snapshot",
28	      "permission-mode"       => "permission_mode",
29	      "queue-operation"       => "queue_operation",
30	    }.freeze
31	
32	    # Harness bookkeeping — records that are not part of the conversation "from
33	    # Jess's perspective". They are still parsed into events (so nothing is lost
34	    # and event_count == line count), but flagged `hidden: true` so the renderer
35	    # skips them. See notes/2026-07-20-session-6-hidden-events.md for the full
36	    # rationale (which types, and why the ones we KEEP are worth keeping).
37	    #
38	    # Whole kinds that are always hidden:
39	    HIDDEN_KINDS = %w[system file_snapshot permission_mode].freeze
40	    # Attachment subtypes that are pure context-loading / hook plumbing. The two
41	    # conversation-relevant attachments stay visible: `queued_command` (delivered
42	    # queued input AND background <task-notification>s — "the agent being nudged")
43	    # and `task_reminder` (the system nudging the agent about pending tasks) —
44	    # except a `task_reminder` with itemCount 0 has nothing to show, so those
45	    # are hidden individually below rather than by type.
46	    HIDDEN_ATTACHMENT_TYPES = %w[
47	      hook_success deferred_tools_delta mcp_instructions_delta skill_listing
48	    ].freeze
49	    # The unsent-prompt buffer (a `last-prompt` record → `unknown` fallback).
50	    HIDDEN_RECORD_TYPES = %w[last-prompt].freeze
51	    # queue-operation and task_notification stay visible — EXCEPT the bare
52	    # `dequeue`/`remove` markers, which are hidden: they carry no content of
53	    # their own, and the event each one delivers gets `dequeued: true` or
54	    # `removed_from_queue: true` instead (see match_delivery! below), so the
55	    # "took a detour through the queue" fact still shows, just on the event
56	    # that actually has something to say.
57	
58	    # A background task result arrives mid-conversation as a plain `user`
59	    # record whose string content is this XML blob — NOT something Jess typed.
60	    TASK_NOTIFICATION_TAG = "<task-notification>"
61	
62	    # tool_use `name` -> which input key is worth surfacing as the one-line
63	    # "primary arg" (in card summaries and the Fields section). Anything not
64	    # listed here shows no primary arg (just the tool name).
65	    PRIMARY_ARG_KEY = {
66	      "Read" => "file_path", "Write" => "file_path", "Edit" => "file_path",
67	      "Bash" => "command", "Grep" => "pattern", "Glob" => "pattern",
68	    }.freeze
69	
70	    # A tool result is the thing that actually grows the context, but the log
71	    # never counts one: `usage` appears on assistant records only. The single
72	    # measured signal is the context delta at the next turn, and in the example
73	    # logs that gap ALWAYS also holds harness records — 0 of 32 gaps contain a
74	    # tool result by itself — so it can't be attributed cleanly. Hence an
75	    # estimate from length. Calibrating against those deltas put the median near
76	    # 2.5 chars/token, but the delta overstates the result's own share (it
77	    # covers the whole gap), and tool output is code and JSON, which tokenizes
78	    # denser than the prose-tuned 4. 3.5 splits the difference. Retune here if a
79	    # better measurement turns up; the renderer labels the number an estimate.
80	    CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.5
81	
82	    ELLIPSIS = "…"
83	    SUMMARY_LIMIT = 140
84	    # user/assistant messages are the actual conversation — the headline
85	    # content of the page — so they get a much longer leash before truncating
86	    # than the "background machinery" kinds (tool calls, thinking, etc).
87	    MESSAGE_SUMMARY_LIMIT = 400
88	
89	    # @param log_path [String] path to the top-level conversation .jsonl.
90	    def initialize(log_path)
91	      @log_path = log_path
92	      @log_file = File.basename(log_path)            # source.file (with .jsonl)
93	      @log_name = File.basename(log_path, ".jsonl")  # the `ref` prefix (no ext)
94	    end
95	
96	    # @return [Hash] the intermediate document (YAML-serializable with string
97	    #   keys and plain scalars only, so YAML.safe_load round-trips it).
98	    def to_document
99	      records = read_records
100	      events  = records.map { |lineno, rec| build_event(lineno, rec) }
101	      link_related_events!(events)
102	      mark_turns!(events)
103	      { "meta" => build_meta(records, events), "events" => events }
104	    end
105	
106	    private
107	
108	    # @return [Array<[Integer, Hash]>] 1-based line number paired with the parsed
109	    #   record. Blank lines are skipped but still advance the line counter, so
110	    #   source.line stays exact against the committed log.
111	    def read_records
112	      out = []
113	      File.foreach(@log_path).with_index(1) do |raw, lineno|
114	        next if raw.strip.empty?
115	        out << [lineno, JSON.parse(raw)]
116	      end
117	      out
118	    end
119	
120	    # ---- one event per record ------------------------------------------------
121	
122	    def build_event(lineno, rec)
123	      kind = kind_for(rec)
124	      event = {
125	        "id"      => rec["uuid"] || "line-#{lineno}",
126	        # a short, human-referable handle built from provenance: "<name>:<line>"
127	        # (e.g. episode-8-before:9). Stable to cite when discussing an event.
128	        "ref"     => "#{@log_name}:#{lineno}",
129	        "agent"   => agent_for(rec),
130	        "parent"  => rec["parentUuid"],
131	        "kind"    => kind,
132	        "role"    => rec.dig("message", "role"),
133	        "at"      => rec["timestamp"],
134	        "summary" => summary_for(kind, rec),
135	        "source"  => { "file" => @log_file, "line" => lineno },
136	      }
137	      event["operation"] = rec["operation"] if kind == "queue_operation"
138	      add_detail(event, kind, rec)
139	      add_assistant_fields(event, rec) if rec["type"] == "assistant"
140	      event["hidden"] = true if hidden?(kind, rec)
141	      event
142	    end
143	
144	    # Is this record harness bookkeeping the renderer should skip? See the
145	    # HIDDEN_* constants above.
146	    def hidden?(kind, rec)
147	      return true if HIDDEN_KINDS.include?(kind)
148	      return true if HIDDEN_RECORD_TYPES.include?(rec["type"])
149	      return true if kind == "attachment" &&
150	                     HIDDEN_ATTACHMENT_TYPES.include?(rec.dig("attachment", "type"))
151	      return true if kind == "attachment" &&
152	                     rec.dig("attachment", "type") == "task_reminder" &&
153	                     rec.dig("attachment", "itemCount").to_i.zero?
154	
155	      false
156	    end
157	
158	    def kind_for(rec)
159	      case rec["type"]
160	      when "user"      then user_kind(rec)
161	      when "assistant" then assistant_kind(rec)
162	      else TYPE_TO_KIND.fetch(rec["type"], "unknown")
163	      end
164	    end
165	
166	    # a tool_result arrives as a user-role record whose content is an array; a
167	    # delivered background-task result arrives as a user-role record whose
168	    # string content is a <task-notification> blob — not something Jess typed.
169	    def user_kind(rec)
170	      content = rec.dig("message", "content")
171	      return "tool_result" if content.is_a?(Array)
172	      return "task_notification" if content.is_a?(String) &&
173	                                     content.strip.start_with?(TASK_NOTIFICATION_TAG)
174	
175	      "user_message"
176	    end
177	
178	    # every assistant record observed carries exactly one content block; its
179	    # type picks the finer-grained kind (tool_use -> tool_call, thinking ->
180	    # thinking, text -> assistant_message). Order matters if that ever changes:
181	    # a tool_use or thinking block is more informative than an empty text block.
182	    def assistant_kind(rec)
183	      blocks = Array(rec.dig("message", "content"))
184	      return "tool_call" if blocks.any? { |b| b["type"] == "tool_use" }
185	      return "thinking" if blocks.any? { |b| %w[thinking redacted_thinking].include?(b["type"]) }
186	
187	      "assistant_message"
188	    end
189	
190	    # (c) prefer an explicit agentId (subagent records carry one); else `main`.
191	    def agent_for(rec)
192	      id = rec["agentId"] || rec.dig("message", "agentId")
193	      id ? "agent-#{id}".sub(/\Aagent-agent-/, "agent-") : "main"
194	    end

196	    # ---- summaries (one line, whitespace collapsed) --------------------------
197	
198	    def summary_for(kind, rec)
199	      case kind
200	      when "user_message"      then truncate(strip_markdown(rec.dig("message", "content").to_s), MESSAGE_SUMMARY_LIMIT)
201	      when "assistant_message" then assistant_summary(rec)
202	      when "thinking"          then thinking_summary(rec)
203	      when "tool_call"         then tool_call_summary(rec)
204	      when "tool_result"       then tool_result_summary(rec)
205	      when "task_notification" then task_notification_summary(rec)
206	      when "system"            then system_summary(rec)
207	      when "attachment"        then attachment_summary(rec)
208	      when "file_snapshot"     then "File history snapshot"
209	      when "permission_mode"   then "Permission mode: #{rec["permissionMode"]}"
210	      when "queue_operation"   then queue_summary(rec)
211	      else                          "#{rec["type"]} record"
212	      end
213	    end
214	
215	    def assistant_summary(rec)
216	      text = Array(rec.dig("message", "content"))
217	             .select { |b| b["type"] == "text" }.map { |b| b["text"] }.join(" ").strip
218	      truncate(strip_markdown(text), MESSAGE_SUMMARY_LIMIT)
219	    end
220	
221	    def thinking_summary(rec)
222	      return "(reasoning — redacted by Anthropic)" if redacted_thinking?(rec)
223	
224	      text = thinking_text(rec).strip
225	      text.empty? ? "(reasoning — not captured)" : truncate(strip_markdown(text))
226	    end
227	
228	    def tool_call_summary(rec)
229	      tu = tool_use_block(rec)
230	      return "Tool call" unless tu
231	
232	      arg = primary_arg(tu["name"], tu["input"] || {})
233	      truncate(arg ? "#{tu["name"]} #{arg}" : tu["name"].to_s)
234	    end
235	
236	    def tool_result_summary(rec)
237	      text = extract_text(rec.dig("message", "content"))
238	      text.empty? ? "Tool result" : truncate(text)
239	    end
240	
241	    # the <summary> field inside the <task-notification> blob is the whole
242	    # point of the notification; showing the raw XML as the summary (the old
243	    # generic behavior) buried it.
244	    def task_notification_summary(rec)
245	      summary_from_task_notification(rec.dig("message", "content").to_s)
246	    end
247	
248	    def summary_from_task_notification(text)
249	      inner = text[%r{<summary>(.*?)</summary>}m, 1]
250	      truncate(inner || text)
251	    end
252	
253	    def system_summary(rec)
254	      sub = rec["subtype"] || "system"
255	      count = rec["hookCount"]
256	      count ? "#{sub} — #{count} hook#{"s" unless count == 1}" : sub
257	    end
258	
259	    # `queued_command` carries the same payload shapes as a top-level
260	    # `task_notification`/`user_message` (it's the same content, just delivered
261	    # via the queue-detour envelope instead) — extract its <summary> the same
262	    # way, so the card doesn't just say the literal type name "queued_command".
263	    def attachment_summary(rec)
264	      att = rec["attachment"] || {}
265	      return queued_command_summary(att) if att["type"] == "queued_command"
266	
267	      label = [att["type"], att["hookName"] || att["hookEvent"]].compact.join(": ")
268	      label.empty? ? "Attachment" : label
269	    end
270	
271	    def queued_command_summary(att)
272	      queued_payload_summary(att["prompt"].to_s)
273	    end
274	
275	    # An `enqueue` carries the payload it is queueing (a message Jess typed while
276	    # the agent was busy, or a background <task-notification>) — that payload is
277	    # the interesting part, so the summary says WHAT got queued, not just that
278	    # something did. `dequeue`/`remove` are bare markers with nothing to show
279	    # (and are hidden anyway), so they keep the short verb.
280	    def queue_summary(rec)
281	      op = rec["operation"] || "queue"
282	      payload = queued_payload_summary(rec["content"].to_s)
283	      payload.empty? ? "Queue #{op}" : truncate("Queue #{op}: #{payload}")
284	    end
285	
286	    # The same payload shapes a `queued_command` attachment carries: either a
287	    # <task-notification> blob (whose <summary> is the point) or plain text.
288	    def queued_payload_summary(content)
289	      return "" if content.strip.empty?
290	      return summary_from_task_notification(content) if content.strip.start_with?(TASK_NOTIFICATION_TAG)
291	
292	      truncate(strip_markdown(content))
293	    end

295	    # ---- detail payload (drill-in) -------------------------------------------
296	    #
297	    # Known kinds get named `detail`/`tool` fields (the renderer reads the
298	    # schema, never the log). Only `unknown` keeps `detail.raw` verbatim.
299	
300	    def add_detail(event, kind, rec)
301	      case kind
302	      when "user_message"
303	        event["detail"] = { "text" => rec.dig("message", "content").to_s }
304	      when "assistant_message"
305	        text = Array(rec.dig("message", "content"))
306	               .select { |b| b["type"] == "text" }.map { |b| b["text"] }.join("\n\n")
307	        event["detail"] = { "text" => text } unless text.strip.empty?
308	      when "thinking"
309	        text = thinking_text(rec)
310	        event["detail"] = { "text" => text } unless text.strip.empty?
311	      when "tool_call"
312	        add_tool_call_fields(event, rec)
313	      when "tool_result"
314	        text = extract_text(rec.dig("message", "content"))
315	        event["detail"] = { "text" => text } unless text.empty?
316	        add_tool_result_fields(event, rec)
317	      when "task_notification"
318	        content = rec.dig("message", "content").to_s
319	        event["detail"] = { "text" => content } unless content.strip.empty?
320	      when "queue_operation"
321	        # `enqueue` carries the queued payload (a queued user message, or a
322	        # background <task-notification> like "…failed with exit code 1").
323	        # `dequeue`/`remove` are bare markers with no content.
324	        content = rec["content"].to_s
325	        event["detail"] = { "text" => content } unless content.strip.empty?
326	      when "attachment"
327	        text = attachment_detail_text(rec)
328	        event["detail"] = { "text" => text } unless text.strip.empty?
329	      when "unknown"
330	        event["detail"] = { "raw" => rec }
331	      end
332	    end
333	
334	    def thinking_text(rec)
335	      Array(rec.dig("message", "content"))
336	        .select { |b| b["type"] == "thinking" }.map { |b| b["thinking"] }.join("\n\n")
337	    end
338	
339	    # A `redacted_thinking` block carries only an encrypted `data` blob (no
340	    # human-readable `thinking` text) — Anthropic redacted the reasoning
341	    # content itself, not just this parser's view of it.
342	    def redacted_thinking?(rec)
343	      Array(rec.dig("message", "content")).any? { |b| b["type"] == "redacted_thinking" }
344	    end
345	
346	    def tool_use_block(rec)
347	      Array(rec.dig("message", "content")).find { |b| b["type"] == "tool_use" }
348	    end
349	
350	    def add_tool_call_fields(event, rec)
351	      tu = tool_use_block(rec)
352	      return unless tu
353	
354	      input = tu["input"] || {}
355	      event["tool"] = { "name" => tu["name"], "use_id" => tu["id"], "input" => input }
356	      arg = primary_arg(tu["name"], input)
357	      event["tool"]["primary_arg"] = arg if arg
358	    end
359	
360	    def primary_arg(name, input)
361	      key = PRIMARY_ARG_KEY[name]
362	      if key && input[key]
363	        # Read/Write/Edit take a file_path; the directory is rarely the
364	        # interesting part of a one-line summary, so show just the filename.
365	        value = key == "file_path" ? File.basename(input[key].to_s) : input[key].to_s
366	        return truncate(value, 90)
367	      end
368	      return input["subagent_type"] || input["description"] if name == "Agent"
369	
370	      nil
371	    end
372	
373	    # (b) named tool-result fields from the record's own content block and its
374	    # sibling `toolUseResult` (durationMs, stdout/stderr, structured_patch…).
375	    def add_tool_result_fields(event, rec)
376	      block = Array(rec.dig("message", "content")).first || {}
377	      tool = { "use_id" => block["tool_use_id"], "is_error" => block.fetch("is_error", false) }
378	
379	      tur = rec["toolUseResult"]
380	      if tur.is_a?(Hash)
381	        tool["duration_ms"] = tur["durationMs"] || tur["totalDurationMs"]
382	        result = {}
383	        result["stdout"]           = tur["stdout"] if tur.key?("stdout")
384	        result["stderr"]           = tur["stderr"] if tur.key?("stderr")
385	        result["interrupted"]      = tur["interrupted"] if tur.key?("interrupted")
386	        result["num_files"]        = tur["numFiles"] if tur.key?("numFiles")
387	        result["structured_patch"] = tur["structuredPatch"] if tur["structuredPatch"]
388	        tool["result"] = result unless result.empty?
389	
390	        if tur["totalTokens"]
391	          tool["subagent_tokens"] = {
392	            "total_tokens"          => tur["totalTokens"],
393	            "total_tool_use_count"  => tur["totalToolUseCount"],
394	          }
395	        end
396	      end
397	      event["tool"] = tool
398	      add_result_token_estimate(event)
399	    end
400	
401	    # What this result added to the context — estimated, because nothing counts
402	    # it (see CHARS_PER_TOKEN). Named `estimated_input` rather than `input` so
403	    # no consumer can mistake it for a number the API reported; the renderer
404	    # prints it with a ≈ and says where it came from.
405	    def add_result_token_estimate(event)
406	      chars = event.dig("detail", "text").to_s.length
407	      return if chars.zero?
408	
409	      event["tokens"] = {
410	        "result_chars"    => chars,
411	        "estimated_input" => (chars / CHARS_PER_TOKEN).round,
412	      }
413	    end
414	
415	    # The human-relevant body of a (visible) attachment: `queued_command` carries
416	    # a `prompt` (the delivered notification/input); other attachments may carry a
417	    # `content` array of text blocks.
418	    def attachment_detail_text(rec)
419	      att = rec["attachment"] || {}
420	      return att["prompt"].to_s if att["prompt"]
421	
422	      extract_text(att["content"])
423	    end
424	
425	    # (b) named token + turn fields on assistant turns.
426	    def add_assistant_fields(event, rec)
427	      msg = rec["message"] || {}
428	      event["model"]         = msg["model"] if msg["model"]
429	      event["stop_reason"]   = msg["stop_reason"]
430	      event["stop_details"]  = msg["stop_details"]
431	      event["stop_sequence"] = msg["stop_sequence"]
432	
433	      # `message.id` is what makes a TURN visible in the schema: the thinking
434	      # record, the text record and each tool_use record of one API response all
435	      # carry it. mark_turns! groups on it, and the renderer uses it to show an
436	      # assistant message the tool calls that came back with it.
437	      event["links"] = { "message_id" => msg["id"] } if msg["id"]
438	
439	      usage = msg["usage"]
440	      return unless usage.is_a?(Hash)
441	
442	      event["tokens"] = {
443	        "input"          => usage["input_tokens"],
444	        "output"         => usage["output_tokens"],
445	        "cache_creation" => usage["cache_creation_input_tokens"],
446	        "cache_read"     => usage["cache_read_input_tokens"],
447	        "ephemeral_1h"   => usage.dig("cache_creation", "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens"),
448	        "ephemeral_5m"   => usage.dig("cache_creation", "ephemeral_5m_input_tokens"),
449	        "service_tier"   => usage["service_tier"],
450	      }
451	    end
452	
453	    # ---- assistant turns -----------------------------------------------------
454	    #
455	    # One API response can span several records — a thinking block, a text
456	    # block, and one record per tool_use, all sharing `message.id` — and EVERY
457	    # one of them repeats the whole turn's `usage`. So token counts are a fact
458	    # about the TURN, not the record: attributing them per record would triple
459	    # count a running total, and would print the same numbers on three cards.
460	    #
461	    # Each turn therefore elects a `turn_leader`, the one record that shows the
462	    # numbers: the assistant_message record when the turn produced prose, and
463	    # the turn's first record otherwise. The fallback is not hypothetical — 7 of
464	    # 33 turns in episode-8-before (11 of 28 in episode-8-after) are bare
465	    # tool_use with no text block, and without it their tokens, and the jump
466	    # they cause in the running total, would appear on no card at all.
467	    def mark_turns!(events)
468	      running = 0
469	      turns(events).each_value do |group|
470	        leader = group.find { |e| e["kind"] == "assistant_message" } || group.first
471	        leader["turn_leader"] = true
472	
473	        tokens = leader["tokens"]
474	        next unless tokens
475	
476	        # The context actually sent this turn: fresh tokens, tokens written to
477	        # the cache, and tokens read back from it. The log's bare `input_tokens`
478	        # is only the uncached remainder — typically 1 or 3, which is why it
479	        # can't be shown on its own as "the context length".
480	        tokens["context"] = %w[input cache_creation cache_read].sum { |k| tokens[k].to_i }
481	        tokens["added"]   = tokens["input"].to_i + tokens["cache_creation"].to_i
482	        running += tokens["context"]
483	        tokens["cumulative_context"] = running
484	      end
485	    end
486	
487	    # message_id => that turn's records, in log order. A record with no message
488	    # id becomes a turn of its own (defensive — none in the example logs).
489	    def turns(events)
490	      events.each_with_object({}) do |e, acc|
491	        next unless e["role"] == "assistant"
492	
493	        id = e.dig("links", "message_id") || "line-#{e.dig("source", "line")}"
494	        (acc[id] ||= []) << e
495	      end
496	    end
497	
498	    # ---- cross-event linking (item 3/10: light up the causal chain together) -
499	    #
500	    # Two independent pairings, both keyed by an id already carried in the log:
501	    #   tool_call <-> tool_result, by the tool_use_id both sides share.
502	    #   queue enqueue <-> dequeue/remove <-> the delivered task_notification,
503	    #   by task-id (from the <task-notification> XML) — dequeue/remove carry no
504	    #   id of their own, so pairing with their enqueue is positional (FIFO,
505	    #   which is exactly what a queue is).
506	    # A shared link_ids token on both events is all the renderer/JS need to
507	    # highlight the whole chain together; the original background tool_call
508	    # joins the chain too, via the tool-use-id embedded in the notification.
509	    def link_related_events!(events)
510	      calls_by_use_id = events.select { |e| e["kind"] == "tool_call" }
511	                               .to_h { |e| [e.dig("tool", "use_id"), e] }
512	
513	      events.each do |e|
514	        next unless e["kind"] == "tool_result"
515	
516	        use_id = e.dig("tool", "use_id")
517	        call = calls_by_use_id[use_id]
518	        next unless call
519	
520	        link!(call, e, "tool:#{use_id}")
521	        name = call.dig("tool", "name")
522	        e["tool"]["name"] = name
523	        resummarize_tool_result!(e, name)
524	      end
525	
526	      link_queue_lifecycle!(events, calls_by_use_id)
527	    end
528	
529	    # The card already carries a "Bash"/"Read"/etc. tool badge, so the summary
530	    # itself doesn't need to repeat the tool name — just the output.
531	    def resummarize_tool_result!(event, name)
532	      return unless name
533	
534	      text = event.dig("detail", "text").to_s
535	      event["summary"] = truncate(text.empty? ? "No output" : text)
536	    end
537	
538	    def link_queue_lifecycle!(events, calls_by_use_id)
539	      pending = []
540	      awaiting_delivery = []
541	      events.each do |e|
542	        case e["kind"]
543	        when "queue_operation"
544	          link_queue_operation!(e, pending, awaiting_delivery, calls_by_use_id)
545	        when "task_notification", "user_message", "attachment"
546	          match_delivery!(e, awaiting_delivery)
547	          link_task_notification!(e, calls_by_use_id) if e["kind"] == "task_notification"
548	        end
549	      end
550	    end
551	
552	    def link_queue_operation!(event, pending, awaiting_delivery, calls_by_use_id)
553	      if event["operation"] == "enqueue"
554	        task_id, tool_use_id = task_notification_ids(event.dig("detail", "text"))
555	        pending << { event: event, task_id: task_id, tool_use_id: tool_use_id,
556	                      content: event.dig("detail", "text") }
557	        return
558	      end
559	
560	      enqueued = pending.shift
561	      return unless enqueued
562	
563	      token = "queue:#{enqueued[:task_id] || "line-#{enqueued[:event].dig("source", "line")}"}"
564	      link!(enqueued[:event], event, token)
565	      link_to_originating_tool!(enqueued[:tool_use_id], calls_by_use_id, enqueued[:event], event)
566	
567	      # A bare `dequeue`/`remove` marker carries no content of its own — it's
568	      # redundant once the event it delivers downstream is tagged
569	      # `dequeued: true` / `removed_from_queue: true` (below), so hide it the
570	      # same way an empty task_reminder is hidden.
571	      event["hidden"] = true
572	      awaiting_delivery << enqueued.merge(token: token, operation: event["operation"])
573	    end
574	
575	    # Finds the event that actually delivers a dequeued/removed item's content
576	    # — a `task_notification` matched by task-id, a `queued_command` attachment
577	    # (also matched by task-id, since it carries the same <task-notification>
578	    # payload through the queue-detour envelope), or (for a plain queued Jess
579	    # message) the next `user_message` with identical text — and tags it
580	    # `dequeued: true` or `removed_from_queue: true` (depending on which marker
581	    # took it off the queue) so the renderer can show it took a detour through
582	    # the queue instead of arriving as this turn's ordinary input.
583	    def match_delivery!(event, awaiting_delivery)
584	      text = event.dig("detail", "text")
585	      task_id = task_notification_ids(text)[0]
586	      idx = awaiting_delivery.index do |pd|
587	        (pd[:task_id] && pd[:task_id] == task_id) || (pd[:content] && pd[:content] == text)
588	      end
589	      return unless idx
590	
591	      pending_item = awaiting_delivery.delete_at(idx)
592	      field = pending_item[:operation] == "remove" ? "removed_from_queue" : "dequeued"
593	      event[field] = true
594	      link_token!(event, pending_item[:token])
595	    end
596	
597	    def link_task_notification!(event, calls_by_use_id)
598	      task_id, tool_use_id = task_notification_ids(event.dig("detail", "text"))
599	      link_token!(event, "queue:#{task_id}") if task_id
600	      link_to_originating_tool!(tool_use_id, calls_by_use_id, event)
601	    end
602	
603	    def link_to_originating_tool!(tool_use_id, calls_by_use_id, *events)
604	      return unless tool_use_id
605	
606	      token = "tool:#{tool_use_id}"
607	      events.each { |e| link_token!(e, token) }
608	      call = calls_by_use_id[tool_use_id]
609	      link_token!(call, token) if call
610	    end
611	
612	    def task_notification_ids(text)
613	      return [nil, nil] unless text
614	
615	      [text[%r{<task-id>(.*?)</task-id>}m, 1], text[%r{<tool-use-id>(.*?)</tool-use-id>}m, 1]]
616	    end
617	
618	    def link!(a, b, token)
619	      link_token!(a, token)
620	      link_token!(b, token)
621	    end
622	
623	    def link_token!(event, token)
624	      return unless event
625	
626	      ids = (event["link_ids"] ||= [])
627	      ids << token unless ids.include?(token)
628	    end
629	
630	    # ---- meta ----------------------------------------------------------------
631	
632	    def build_meta(records, events)
633	      recs = records.map { |_lineno, rec| rec }
634	      {
635	        "source"      => @log_file,
636	        "name"        => File.basename(@log_path, ".jsonl"),
637	        "session_id"  => first_present(recs, "sessionId"),
638	        "git_branch"  => first_present(recs, "gitBranch"),
639	        "cwd"         => first_present(recs, "cwd"),
640	        "version"     => first_present(recs, "version"),
641	        "model"       => events.map { |e| e["model"] }.compact.first,
642	        "started_at"  => events.map { |e| e["at"] }.compact.first,
643	        "ended_at"    => events.map { |e| e["at"] }.compact.last,
644	        "timezone"    => "UTC",
645	        "event_count" => events.size,
646	        "total_tokens" => total_tokens(events),
647	        "agents"      => build_agents,
648	      }
649	    end
650	
651	    # What the whole conversation cost: every turn's full input context plus
652	    # everything that turn generated. One number for the story — the page
653	    # header's TOKENS stat. nil when no assistant turn carries usage.
654	    #
655	    # Counted once per TURN, which is the only reason this sum means anything:
656	    # the several records of one response each repeat its usage, so summing
657	    # records would multiply the total (see mark_turns!). Note this is token
658	    # USE, not a context size — most of it is the same context re-sent and
659	    # mostly cache-read each turn, which is why the header calls it Tokens.
660	    def total_tokens(events)
661	      leaders = events.select { |e| e["turn_leader"] && e["tokens"] }
662	      return nil if leaders.empty?
663	
664	      leaders.sum { |e| e["tokens"]["context"].to_i + e["tokens"]["output"].to_i }
665	    end
666	
667	    def first_present(recs, key)
668	      recs.each { |r| return r[key] if r[key] }
669	      nil
670	    end
671	
672	    # meta.agents: `main` plus every subagent described by a sibling
673	    # subagents/*.meta.json. Mountain 1 lists them but does not yet inline their
674	    # events (that's the `subagent` kind / nested story, a later mountain).
675	    def build_agents
676	      agents = [{ "id" => "main" }]
677	      dir = File.join(File.dirname(@log_path),
678	                      File.basename(@log_path, ".jsonl"), "subagents")
679	      Dir.glob(File.join(dir, "*.meta.json")).sort.each do |meta_path|
680	        meta = JSON.parse(File.read(meta_path))
681	        id = File.basename(meta_path, ".meta.json") # e.g. agent-ae20659fd0f63295e
682	        agents << {
683	          "id"          => id,
684	          "agent_type"  => meta["agentType"],
685	          "description" => meta["description"],
686	        }
687	      rescue JSON::ParserError
688	        next
689	      end
690	      agents
691	    end
692	
693	    # ---- text helpers --------------------------------------------------------
694	
695	    # Collapse all whitespace to single spaces and cut to one readable line.
696	    def truncate(str, limit = SUMMARY_LIMIT)
697	      s = str.to_s.gsub(/\s+/, " ").strip
698	      s.length > limit ? "#{s[0, limit - 1].rstrip}#{ELLIPSIS}" : s
699	    end
700	
701	    # Cosmetic-only cleanup for one-line plain-text summaries: strip the markdown
702	    # markup itself (not just leave it as literal asterisks/backticks), so a
703	    # truncated summary never shows a stray unmatched `**` or backtick. The full
704	    # text still gets real markdown rendering in the detail view (see
705	    # ConversationStory::Markdown) — this is only for the compact summary line.
706	    def strip_markdown(text)
707	      text.to_s
708	          .gsub(/^\#{1,6}\s+/, "")
709	          .gsub(/^[-*]\s+/, "")
710	          .gsub(/^\d+\.\s+/, "")
711	          .gsub(/```[^\n]*\n?/, "")
712	          .gsub(/(\*\*|__)(.+?)\1/, '\2')
713	          .gsub(/(?<![\w*])[*_]([^*_\n]+)[*_](?!\w)/, '\1')
714	          .gsub(/`([^`]+)`/, '\1')
715	    end
716	
717	    # tool_result content is either a String or an array of {type:text, text:…}
718	    # (and occasionally other block types we ignore for the summary).
719	    def extract_text(content)
720	      case content
721	      when String then content
722	      when Array
723	        content.flat_map do |block|
724	          next block unless block.is_a?(Hash)
725	
726	          inner = block["content"] || block["text"]
727	          inner.is_a?(Array) ? extract_text(inner) : inner
728	        end.compact.join("\n").strip
729	      else ""
730	      end
731	    end
732	  end
733	end
734
